key_insight: QDIFF tests quantum software stacks by comparing output distributions from program variants generated through semantics-preserving transformations.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports testing quantum languages, compilers, simulators, and hardware execution while filtering circuits unlikely to yield useful hardware tests.
method: Generate equivalent program variants using source-to-source transformations.
Filter hardware tests using circuit depth, two-qubit operations, gate error rates, and T1 relaxation time.
Check output-distribution equivalence with extensible comparisons such as Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests and cross entropy.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes the testing design but reports no quantitative evaluation, bug counts, or measured speedups.
watch_item: Probabilistic outputs and hardware noise make equivalence checks sensitive to sampling budgets and comparison thresholds.
paper_title: QDiff: Differential Testing of Quantum Software Stacks
